heard: A dead star can hide inside a living giant star. To our telescopes, the host looks like an ordinary red supergiant, but gas friction drags a swallowed neutron star toward the center. Falling gas heats up to nearly 1 billion Kelvin. This extreme heat forces rapid proton capture inside the stellar belly. Violent convection churns rare rubidium and molybdenum toward the surface. The ravenous core keeps devouring gas and growing heavier. Eventually, that hidden dead core collapses into a black hole. Nothing survives once a dead star grows deep inside.
